construction_markdown:
Let `p(Z)=Z^16+Z^5+Z^3+Z^2+1`, let `F=F_2[Z]/(p)`, and put `α=Z mod p`. Write each `z∈F` uniquely as `z=Σ_{i=0}^{15}z_i α^i`.

Take the deterministically ordered evaluation set `A={Σ_{i=0}^{14}a_iα^i:a_i∈F_2}`, of size `2^15`. For `y=(y_1,…,y_15)∈F_2^15`, define `H(z)_y=z_0+Σ_{i=1}^{15}z_i y_i`, with `y` in binary-integer order.

For every polynomial `f(X)=Σ_{j=0}^{64}b_jX^j∈F[X]`, define

`c_f=(H(f(a))_y)_{(a,y)∈A×F_2^15}`,

ordering first by the binary index of `a` and then by that of `y`. Set `C={c_f:deg f≤64}`. This is the coordinatewise concatenation of the shortened Reed–Solomon code `[32768,65,32704]_{2^16}` with the affine code `RM(1,15)=[32768,16,16384]_2`. It uses no randomness, padding, puncturing, or unspecified finite choice.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: For binary linear codes `C_i` of dimensions at least two, the average-weight bound gives `d_i/n_i≤2/3`. Since `d(C_1⊗C_2)=d_1d_2`, every ordinary tensor product with two nontrivial factors has relative distance at most `4/9<511/1024`. If at most one factor has dimension above one, tensoring preserves that factor's dimension. Thus ordinary binary Kronecker products cannot manufacture a leaderboard improvement.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: The scalar-orbit lemma from algebraic-09 extends from `RM(1,15)` to arbitrary coordinate-dependent binary-linear inner maps `F_{2^16}→F_2^32768`. Averaging all nonzero inner symbols gives at most `16384·65536/65535` weight per supported outer coordinate. Singleton then shows any field-linear outer dimension `K≥66` has a scalar multiple below the target. Hence the entire equal-block field-linear architecture is capped at `16·65=1040`.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: Does there exist a deterministic binary `[16384,16,d≥8185]` or `[8192,17,d≥4090]` code with a complete distance proof? The first would give at least `k=1168` using a full-length `F_{2^16}` Reed–Solomon outer code; the second gives `k=1105` using `[131072,65,131008]_{2^17}`. The Griesmer endpoint `[16384,16,8191]` is impossible, but distances `8185,…,8190` remain a precise finite bottleneck.

proof_markdown:
# Exact Reed–Solomon–affine product code

## Theorem

There is a symbolically deterministic binary linear code with exact parameters

`[1073741824,1040,535822336]_2`.

Moreover, 1040 is maximal within the architecture consisting of an arbitrary `F_{2^16}`-linear outer code of length 32768 and coordinate-dependent injective binary-linear inner maps of length 32768.

## Explicit field

Let `p(Z)=Z^16+Z^5+Z^3+Z^2+1`. Repeated squaring modulo `p` gives

`Z^(2^8) ≡ Z^8+Z^7+Z^3+Z`, and `Z^(2^16) ≡ Z`.

Put `h=Z^8+Z^7+Z^3`, the residue of `Z^(2^8)+Z`. Direct polynomial division over `F_2` gives

`p=(Z^8+Z^7+Z^6+Z^5+Z^4+Z^2+1)h+(Z^2+1)`,

`h=(Z^6+Z^5+Z^4+Z^3+Z^2+1)(Z^2+1)+1`.

Thus `gcd(p,Z^(2^8)+Z)=1`, while `p` divides `Z^(2^16)+Z`. Every irreducible factor of `p` therefore has degree dividing 16, and none has degree dividing 8. Since every proper divisor of 16 divides 8 and `deg p=16`, `p` is irreducible. Hence `F=F_2[Z]/(p)` is the explicitly represented field of order `2^16`.

## Construction, linearity, length, and dimension

Let `α=Z mod p`, and write `z=Σ_{i=0}^{15}z_iα^i`. Define

`A=span_{F_2}{1,α,…,α^14}`

and

`H(z)_y=z_0+Σ_{i=1}^{15}z_i y_i`, for `y∈F_2^15`.

The map `H` is binary linear. Its coordinate at `y=0` recovers `z_0`, and comparison with its coordinates at the unit vectors recovers `z_1,…,z_15`; hence it is injective.

For `f∈F[X]` of degree at most 64, set `c_f=(H(f(a)))_{a∈A}` and let `C` be the set of all such words. Evaluation and `H` are binary linear, so `C` is binary linear. There are `2^15` blocks, each of length `2^15`, giving exact length `2^30`.

The message space has dimension 65 over `F`, hence binary dimension 1040. The encoder is injective: if `c_f=0`, injectivity of `H` gives `f(a)=0` for all 32,768 elements of `A`; the polynomial root bound then forces `f=0`. Thus `dim_{F_2}C=1040`.

## Minimum distance

If `f` is nonzero, it has at most 64 roots in `A`, so at least 32,704 blocks are nonzero. If `z∉{0,1}`, the linear part of `H(z)` is nonzero and its truth table is balanced, of weight `2^14`. The symbol `1` gives the all-one block of weight `2^15`. Therefore every nonzero block weighs at least `2^14`, and every nonzero codeword satisfies

`wt(c_f)≥32704·2^14=2^29-2^20=535822336`.

This bound is attained deterministically. Let

`B=span_{F_2}{1,α,…,α^5}⊂A`, so `|B|=64`,

and put `g(X)=∏_{b∈B}(X-b)`. For `a∈A\B`, `g(a)≠0`. At most 32,704 scalars are forbidden by the equations `λg(a)=1`, whereas `|F*|=65,535`. Choose the nonzero `λ` of least polynomial-basis binary index outside `{g(a)^(-1):a∈A\B}`. Then `λg` has exactly the 64 roots in `B`, and every surviving value is neither zero nor one. Hence its 32,704 surviving blocks are all balanced and

`wt(c_{λg})=32704·2^14=535822336`.

Thus the minimum distance is exact.

## Scalar-orbit ceiling for the equal-block field-linear architecture

Let `Q=2^m`, and let `φ:F_Q→F_2^L` be any binary-linear map. Across `F_Q*`, each nonzero output coordinate of `φ` is one on exactly `Q/2` inputs, while a zero coordinate contributes nothing. Consequently

`(1/(Q-1)) Σ_{z∈F_Q*} wt(φ(z)) ≤ LQ/(2(Q-1))`.

Now let an `F_Q`-linear outer code have length `N` and dimension `K`, with arbitrary coordinate-dependent maps `φ_j`. Singleton supplies a nonzero outer word supported on at most `N-K+1` coordinates. Averaging all its nonzero scalar multiples therefore shows that some concatenated word has weight at most

`(N-K+1)LQ/(2(Q-1))`.

For `Q=65536`, `N=L=32768`, and `K=66`, this is

`32703·16384·65536/65535 < 32704·16384`;

the cross-multiplied gap is `32704·65535-32703·65536=32832>0`. Thus `K≥66` violates the target, so this entire architecture has binary dimension at most `16·65=1040`. The submitted code attains the ceiling.

## Ordinary tensor-product obstruction

For a binary `[n,k,d]` linear code, summing weights over all codewords gives

`(2^k-1)d≤n2^(k-1)`.

Thus if `k≥2`, `d/n≤2^(k-1)/(2^k-1)≤2/3`. For two binary linear codes, the Kronecker product has length `n_1n_2`, dimension `k_1k_2`, and exact distance `d_1d_2`: every nonzero product-code matrix has at least `d_2` nonzero columns, each of weight at least `d_1`, while a tensor of minimum words attains the product. Hence two factors of dimension at least two have relative distance at most `4/9<511/1024`. Additional factors cannot repair this. If only one factor has dimension above one, all other factors are one-dimensional and the total dimension is unchanged.

## Endpoint obstruction for a stronger inner constituent

More generally, no binary code `[2^r,r+2,2^(r-1)-1]_2` exists for `r≥3`. The residual proof of the Griesmer inequality gives equality at these parameters and excludes distance `2^(r-1)`. Residualizing at a minimum word gives `[2^(r-1)+1,r+1,2^(r-2)]`; puncturing one coordinate preserves dimension and yields the same hypothetical family with `r` replaced by `r-1`. Iteration gives `[8,5,3]_2`, but its disjoint radius-one Hamming balls would require `2^5(1+8)≤2^8`, which is false.

Taking `r=14` rules out `[16384,16,8191]_2`, and therefore rules out the tempting hypothetical `k=1936` Reed–Solomon concatenation. It does not rule out distances 8185 through 8190, which remain concrete finite constituent-code questions.

The construction and all scoped obstructions above are proved, but the campaign entry should remain under review until independently accepted.
